activities.anchor: decides drying, reworking, luminosity and survival
activities.caption: which binder runs which paint
activities.name: medBindMatch

config.prompt: Each medium is a binder with a personality — pair binder to paint:

pairs.right: watercolour — pigment and binder absorbed into sized paper
acrylic — droplets of plastic suspended in water
oil paint — polymerising over days to months
egg tempera — the panel tradition of the 13th–15th centuries
encaustic — translucent colour fused with heat

config.why: The binder decides how the colour dries, how it can be reworked, how light enters it and how long it survives — the same ultramarine is luminous in watercolour, flat in gouache, jewel-like in oil glaze.

activities.caption: bet the transmission of a three-glaze stack
activities.name: medGlazeEst

config.prompt: Three magenta glazes each transmit roughly two-thirds of the light that reaches them. Roughly what percentage of the light gets through all three?
config.why: (2/3)³ ≈ 30% — each transparent layer subtracts light where palette mixing adds scattering; the result is a deep, still-luminous crimson impossible to mix on the palette.
config.context: about (2/3)³ ≈ 30% transmission — a stacked, still-luminous crimson

config.prompt: Acrylic dries by coalescence — put the clock in order:
items: Pigment sits as droplets of plastic suspended in water
Droplets fuse into a continuous flexible film
The film is permanently waterproof — layer light over dark, overpaint anything
config.why: Minutes of workability, then permanent waterproofing: retarders and stay-wet palettes extend the open blending window, but nothing extends it to oil's scale.

activities.caption: before the tube / after the tube
activities.name: medTubeCompare

config.prompt: One container, one art movement — drag the divider:

before.label: before 1841
before.text: pigments live in fragile bladders that must be punctured and used fast — the studio is where painting happens

after.label: after Rand's tin tube
after.text: pre-mixed, portable colour leaves for the riverbank — the Impressionists build their method on outdoor observation of changing light, and Renoir credits the tube as a precondition of the movement

config.why: A container changed an art history: the medium's properties, down to its packaging, are part of the expressive decision.

config.prompt: Two aesthetics and one clock, all from the same paint — file each statement:

items.label: thin transparent colour over a dry underpainting
the old masters' flesh tones — light returns twice-filtered
linseed oxygen-cross-links into a solid translucent network over days to months
earth colours and lead driers speed the clock; whites and blacks slow it

config.why: Direct and indirect are two complete aesthetics from the same oil paint; depth is light penetrating the glaze, reflecting from the underlayer and returning twice-filtered.

activities.caption: true or false — oil vs watercolour difficulty
activities.name: medFailJudge

statements.s: Oil is 'stronger' than watercolour and therefore easier.
statements.why: It is easier to correct and harder to judge — colours shift as they dry, values deepen over months, and layer-structure mistakes surface decades later.

statements.s: Watercolour's difficulty is instantaneous; oil's is deferred.
statements.why: Watercolour punishes hesitation in the moment; oil's structural mistakes can wait decades to appear.

statements.s: Oil glazes read wetter than they will dry.
statements.why: Colours shift as the film dries — part of why oil is harder to judge.

statements.s: A mistake in oil's layer structure shows up in the same session.
statements.why: It surfaces decades later — the deferred difficulty.

activities.caption: match the specialist medium to its signature
activities.name: medSpecMatch

config.prompt: Each specialist binder pushes one property to its extreme — match them:

pairs.right: watercolour made opaque — flat, matte, even colour that re-wets and rewelds
dries in seconds — form built from fine hatched strokes over gesso
pigmented beeswax fused with heat — translucent layers you can scrape back into
every medium simulated, with unlimited undo

config.why: Flat opacity, hatched patience, scrapeable translucency, unlimited undo — friction teaches judgement, and students who never commit never develop the commitment muscles.

activities.anchor: the difference between muddy and luminous mixes
activities.caption: chart the pigment's bias
activities.name: medBiasCloze

config.text: Test boards swatch every new pigment's %%0%%, opacity and drying behaviour before it touches the work; colour charts expose each pigment's bias — ultramarine leans %%1%%, phthalo leans %%2%%.
config.hint: Knowing which blue makes which green is the working distinction.
